Subject: Production errors: generation 503s + timeouts — are you seeing this?

Hi Vanessa,

We're seeing a spike of 503s and high tail latency from the Redwood dedicated endpoint for Acme Retail starting ~08:00 PST. Requests that were previously 200 in <300ms are now returning 503 or timing out after retries. This affects our checkout assistant (model: rdx-large-8q) and an embedding pipeline.

Can you confirm whether this is an active incident on your side or something we should change on our end? We're stuck on a release window and this outage is blocking traffic.

Example error: "upstream 503: kernel timeout, kv-cache thrash"

Thanks,
Megan

Hi Megan — thank you for the heads up and the screenshot. We're seeing correlated alerts from our dedicated pool in us-west2 (Acme's reserved capacity) and a small fraction of requests are being rejected during autoscale bursts.

Short, immediate actions we are taking now (we've opened an ops incident and engineering is on-call):
- Forcing canary fallback to a hosted-compatible variant for non-sensitive routes to reduce pressure on the pool (ETA 12 min).
- Temporarily lowering batch size for your streaming endpoint to reduce per-request memory pressure.
- Enabling a short-lived soft-capacity to allow limited burst traffic while we investigate.

Can you confirm whether you can tolerate a hosted fallback for the next 30–60 minutes for the checkout assistant? If not, we'll prioritize the dedicated remediation path and keep you updated every 30 minutes.

I'll loop in our account and SRE leads for the full mitigation plan.

—Vanessa

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors: generation 503s + timeouts — Acme Retail (urgent)

Quick technical summary from SRE triage:
- Root cause hypothesis: transient quota pressure + kernel scheduling issue on a subset of reserved nodes that were recently patched. During the autoscale event the newly provisioned nodes failed to warm their KV caches quickly, causing cache misses, elevated GPU memory churn, and a minority of 503s when request windows overlapped with kernel warmup.
- Impact window: 08:00–08:40 PST, with intermittent reoccurrences around autoscale triggers.
- Immediate mitigations applied: host fallback (partial), reduced batch sizes, priority routing for live checkout traffic to reserved warm nodes.
- Next steps (engineering): roll back the hot-patch to affected host image, force warm cache on a small subset, and add a short-lived rate-smoothing throttle to avoid simultaneous large batch submissions during autoscale.

We estimate full restoration on dedicated pool stability in ~2–3 hours if the rollback and cache-warm ops go cleanly. We'll post timeline updates.

—Marissa

Subject: Post-incident summary + next steps (Acme Retail dedicated pool incident)

Megan — thanks again for your patience while we worked through the dedicated-capacity instability. This is a short post-incident summary and next steps; we'll follow up with a formal RCA doc and an invite for a 1-hour joint review.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2027-11-08 08:00–08:40 PST with intermittent reoccurrences during autoscale triggers; primary customer impact felt during your release window.
- Root cause: A recent image patch on a subset of reserved nodes caused slower KV-cache warmups during autoscale. Combined with simultaneous large-batch submissions this led to elevated GPU memory churn and a minority of rejected requests (503) during warmup windows.
- Action taken: Rolled back the patch on affected hosts, forced KV cache warm on a controlled subset, temporarily lowered batch sizes, and applied a rate-smoothing throttle while autoscale completed. Hosted fallback was used for lower-sensitivity routes to restore user-facing traffic faster.
- Recovery ETA and status: Dedicated pool returned to stable operation by 11:30 PST on 2027-11-08. No further dedicated-pool 503 spikes were observed after stabilization.

Customer impact & remediation offer:
- We will provide a credit for the impacted window and a discretionary goodwill credit; Ben will share estimate by EOD.
- We're scheduling a 1-hour joint RCA on 2027-11-12 10:00 PST to review detailed metrics, change timeline, and preventative work.

Follow-up actions (owner / ETA):
- Formal RCA doc with kernel trace and warmup graphs (Marissa / 2027-11-11 EOD)
- Change freeze and extra validation gating for host image patches affecting reserved nodes (Engineering Policy / 2027-12-01)
- Runbook update: add explicit KV-warm steps and an autoscale smoothing knob (Operations / 2027-11-20)

Attachments: incident_snapshot_20271108.png, mitigation-checklist.pdf
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Acme-Retail-Incident-2027-11, HubSpot record HS-54210
